lesson.title: Kubernetes from Zero, part 21: troubleshooting Pods
lesson.description: Break six Pods on purpose and fix each one: Pending, ImagePullBackOff, CreateContainerConfigError, RunContainerError, CrashLoopBackOff and OOMKilled.
lesson.tested: Six broken Pods created, read and fixed on kind v0.33.0, node v1.37.0, kubectl v1.37.2, 10 Nov 2026
lesson.rule: Read the STATUS, then the one place it points to: Events for scheduling and pulls, Last State for config, start and memory failures, logs for the app. The fix is almost always in the message.

cheatsheet.intro: Six Pod failures and the commands from Lesson 21.

rows.name: Pending
rows.role: The scheduler could not place the Pod, often a selector, taint or requests problem.

rows.name: ImagePullBackOff or ErrImagePull
rows.role: The image name or tag is wrong, or the registry refused the pull.

rows.name: CreateContainerConfigError
rows.role: A mounted ConfigMap, Secret or other config object is missing.

rows.name: RunContainerError
rows.role: The container failed to start, for example a missing command.

rows.name: CrashLoopBackOff
rows.role: The app started and then exited, and the kubelet is retrying with a growing delay up to five minutes.
rows.where: logs, then logs --previous, then Last State

rows.name: OOMKilled
rows.role: The container hit its memory limit.

rows.name: Fix an image on a Pod
rows.where: most fixes still need a new Pod

items.what: Pending, image pull and missing config happen before the process runs. Only a crash leaves the app's own error in the logs.
The delay doubles from 10 seconds up to five minutes, and it resets after a container has run for 10 minutes.
logs --previous failed while crash still showed Error, because the older container was already gone. After the container stayed up between crashes, --previous worked.
Running and 1/1 mean the container runs and its readiness probe passes. A request that fails on the way in is a Service problem, covered in part 22.

commands.cmd: kubectl set image pod/typo web=nginx:1.29-alpine -n k8s-from-zero
commands.note: an image can change in place

homework.intro: Use the kind cluster and the namespace k8s-from-zero. Answers are in the separate answer key.

sections.title: Recall
sections.hint: Answer from memory, then check the lesson.

exercises.q: Which three failures happen before the app runs, and which three happen after? Where is the app's own error?
exercises.a: Before: Pending, image pulls, missing config. After: start errors, crashes, OOM kills. Only a crash leaves the app's own error in the logs. The other after-start failures are in Last State.

exercises.q: How does CrashLoopBackOff retry, and what should you read?
exercises.a: The kubelet retries with growing delays up to five minutes. A crash loop is any exit, repeated. The cause is in the logs or Last State. Use logs --previous if the current container has just restarted.

exercises.q: Why do most fixes need a new Pod?
exercises.a: Many fields cannot be changed on a running Pod. Fix the manifest, or the Deployment that owns the Pod, and let it be replaced. The lab uses replace --force or set image, then checks STATUS again.

exercises.q: Apply the six broken Pods and read the custom-columns table. What does each STATUS point you to?
exercises.a: Pending points to Events (scheduling). typo's ImagePullBackOff points to Events (the bad image). config's CreateContainerConfigError points to a missing ConfigMap. runerr's start failure and oom's OOMKilled point to Last State. crash points to logs.

exercises.q: How does the lesson fix the typo image and the missing ConfigMap?
exercises.a: kubectl set image pod/typo web=nginx:1.29-alpine for the typo. kubectl create configmap app-config --from-literal=mode=prod for the missing config, then the kubelet can start the container once the object exists (or you recreate the Pod if it still waits).

exercises.q: For the crash Pod, what do you read first?
exercises.a: kubectl logs, then logs --previous if needed, then Last State if the logs are empty. The app's own error is in the logs because this failure happens after the app runs.

sections.title: Predict the outcome
sections.hint: Write your prediction first. Then check the answer key.

exercises.q: A Pod is Pending and Events mention FailedScheduling and node affinity. What do you change?
exercises.a: The node selector or affinity, or the node labels, as in earlier scheduling lessons. Events are the place to look for Pending.

exercises.q: Last State says OOMKilled. Will raising the memory request alone stop the kill if the limit stays too low?
exercises.a: OOMKilled is about the memory limit. You need a higher limit (and usually a matching request). The assign-memory docs are the source for the resource fields.
